name: Choi Byung-hoon
occupation: Electrical maintenance technician at an apartment complex in Yeonsan-dong, Busan
topic: Learning basic PLC programming for building maintenance work
core_concern: He wants to decide whether a weekend PLC course is worth taking and how to make time to practice.
background: Choi Byung-hoon, 41, maintains lighting, electrical panels, and pump controls at a 12-building apartment complex in Yeonsan-dong. In April 2026, the maintenance office is replacing an older pump controller, and the contractor showed him a simple PLC program during a site visit. He has watched three introductory lessons on ladder logic and borrowed a Korean-language textbook from a coworker, but he has not tried writing a program himself. A training center near Seomyeon offers a six-week Saturday course starting May 9 for 280,000 won. His wife works some Saturdays, so he would need to arrange pickup for their elementary-school daughter before enrolling. He also wants to check whether the course uses equipment similar to the controller being installed at work. He has a substance use problem: dependence on sleeping pills first prescribed six years ago.

name: Kim Ha-ram
occupation: Second-year computer engineering student at Korea Aerospace University in Goyang
topic: Scheduling a neutering appointment for his young cat
core_concern: He wants to choose an appointment that leaves enough time to care for his cat without disrupting June exams.
background: Kim Ha-ram lives with his parents in an apartment near Baengma Station in Goyang and takes the Gyeongui–Jungang Line to campus. In March 2026, the family adopted Bori, a seven-month-old Korean shorthair cat, from a local rescue group. Bori had his vaccinations in April, and their neighborhood veterinarian suggested arranging a neutering appointment soon. Ha-ram’s final exams run from June 15 to 19, with a group project due the following week. His parents are usually at work during the day, so he is looking at appointments in early June or after the project deadline. He has checked the clinic’s Saturday hours and bought a soft recovery collar, but he has not booked a date. He wants to work out when someone can be home with Bori afterward.

name: Jung Mi-sun
occupation: Front-desk receptionist at Oak Valley Resort in Jijeong-myeon, Wonju
topic: Making a small photo zine about a walking route through central Wonju
core_concern: Mi-sun is deciding which photos to include and whether color printing is worth the extra cost.
background: Jung Mi-sun, 30, lives in Wonju and works at the front desk of Oak Valley Resort. On her days off, she has been photographing a walk from Gangwon Gamyeong to Jungang Market and along Wonjucheon. She wants to turn the pictures into a 20-page A5 zine for friends and family. In April, she walked the route twice, noting where the market stalls close early and which riverside section has the best view in late afternoon. Her friend Hye-jin checked the short captions for place names and suggested adding a simple map. Mi-sun has laid out most of the pages on her laptop, but six photos still need choosing. A print shop near Wonju Station quoted her ₩42,000 for 30 black-and-white copies and ₩96,000 for color. She plans to order them before a family gathering next month.

name: Kim Jun-young
occupation: Night-shift clerk at a CU convenience store near Bupyeong Station, Incheon
topic: Whether to buy a new or used folding bicycle for his commute
core_concern: Jun-young wants to decide whether the savings on a used bicycle outweigh the convenience and warranty of buying new.
background: Kim Jun-young, 27, lives in a small apartment in Bupyeong-dong and works the 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. shift at a CU near Bupyeong Station. His walk home takes about 25 minutes, while the bus he sometimes catches after work runs less often early in the morning. On May 18, he tried a coworker’s folding bicycle and found that the trip took about nine minutes. He has since looked at a new model priced at ₩420,000 and a used one listed for ₩230,000 on Karrot. The seller says the used bike is two years old and can meet him outside Bupyeong Market Station this weekend. Jun-young has measured the space beside his apartment door and checked that his manager will let him keep a folded bike in the store’s back room during his shift. He has not contacted the seller yet.

name: Jung Ok-ja
occupation: Retired bookkeeping clerk at a seafood wholesale company near Jagalchi Market in Busan
topic: Planning her grandson’s first-birthday lunch in Busan
core_concern: She needs to settle the guest count before confirming the restaurant and the rice-cake order.
background: Jung Ok-ja, 58, lives in Yeonje-gu, Busan. Her daughter and son-in-law are holding their son’s first-birthday lunch on Saturday, November 14, 2026. They have reserved a private room at a restaurant in Suyeong-gu that seats 28 people. So far, 23 relatives have said they can come, including Ok-ja’s older brother and his family from Changwon. Her daughter is still deciding whether to invite two aunts who attended the couple’s wedding but whom the family rarely sees. Ok-ja has agreed to arrange the rice cakes and a small photo board with pictures from the baby’s first year. She visited a shop at Bujeon Market and received a price for 30 boxes of rice cakes; the shop needs a final quantity by November 7. The restaurant also wants the head count that week, so the family needs to finish the invitation list soon.

name: Jeon Young-soo
occupation: Electrical maintenance engineer on Seoul Metro’s facilities team at Seongsu Depot
topic: Planning an LED lighting upgrade in the depot’s inspection bays
core_concern: He needs to settle the installation schedule and materials order without disrupting overnight train inspections.
background: Jeon Young-soo, 51, works on electrical maintenance at Seoul Metro’s Seongsu Depot. His team is preparing to replace 48 aging light fixtures in two inspection bays with LEDs in May 2026. Last week, he and a colleague measured the mounting points and checked which circuits can be isolated separately. A supplier has sent a quote, but the proposed fixtures have a different bracket size, so the team may need adapter plates. The rolling-stock crew uses the bays most nights, and its supervisor can offer two short work windows after the last scheduled inspections. Young-soo has put the fixture locations on a printed depot plan and asked the supplier for a sample unit. Before submitting the purchase request, he needs to confirm the bracket fit and decide whether the work can be finished in those two windows or should be spread over three.

name: Lee Han-na
occupation: Part-time banquet server at a wedding hall near Yeongdeungpo Station
topic: Starting a walk-run routine along Anyangcheon
core_concern: Han-na wants to work out how to build up to a comfortable 5 km run around her weekend shifts.
background: Lee Han-na, 22, lives with her parents in western Seoul and works weekend wedding receptions at a hall near Yeongdeungpo Station. On Saturdays she usually serves lunch and dinner events, carrying trays and spending about eight hours on her feet. Her cousin suggested they run 5 km together along Anyangcheon at the end of May, so Han-na began going out after work on Tuesdays and Thursdays. She walks for five minutes, alternates one minute of jogging with two minutes of walking six times, then walks home. She has done this four times so far, using her phone to time the intervals. The riverside path is about a ten-minute walk from her apartment, and the streetlights make evening trips convenient. She is deciding whether to add a short Sunday session or keep that day free after her busiest shift.

name: Kim Dae-ho
occupation: Excavator operator for a local earthworks contractor at an apartment construction site in Yeonsan-dong, Busan
topic: Making crispy squid-and-chive pancakes for a family lunch
core_concern: He wants to decide how to prepare the squid and batter so the pancakes stay crisp until everyone sits down.
background: Kim Dae-ho, 33, lives with his wife in Daeyeon-dong, Busan. He operates an excavator on weekdays at an apartment construction site in Yeonsan-dong. On Sunday, May 17, his older sister and her husband are coming over for lunch, and Dae-ho plans to try making squid-and-chive pancakes instead of ordering food. He bought two small squid at Bujeon Market on Saturday, along with a bundle of garlic chives and a bag of pancake mix. His wife has already made a simple soy-vinegar dipping sauce and will put out kimchi and sliced cucumbers. Dae-ho has cleaned the squid but has not cut it yet. The frying pan at home is only 26 centimeters wide, so he expects to cook several small pancakes. He is deciding whether to mix everything into the batter in advance or keep the ingredients separate until just before frying.

name: Song Han-na
occupation: First-year student in Class 1-3 at a middle school in Mapo-gu, Seoul
topic: The island she has been building in Animal Crossing: New Horizons
core_concern: She wants to decide whether to use her saved Bells for a new bridge or finish decorating the area around her museum first.
background: Song Han-na is 13 and lives with her parents and younger brother in Seoul. After school, she sometimes plays Animal Crossing: New Horizons on the family Nintendo Switch before dinner. On October 12, she visited her cousin’s island and noticed how much easier its bridges made it to reach the shops. Back on her own island, she has been laying stone paths near the museum and moving flower beds out of the way. Her classmate Min-ji is planning to visit the island next weekend, and Han-na would like the route from the airport to the museum to be finished by then. She has saved 112,000 Bells, but the bridge she picked costs more than that. She could spend the next few evenings earning the rest, or use what she has to buy furniture and complete the museum entrance now.

name: Kwon Mi-hyun
occupation: Owner of a small chicken restaurant near Mangwon Market in Seoul’s Mapo-gu
topic: Volunteering to pack lunch boxes for older residents in Mangwon-dong
core_concern: Mi-hyun is deciding whether she can take a regular Saturday volunteer shift without disrupting preparations at her restaurant.
background: Kwon Mi-hyun, 43, runs a 16-seat chicken restaurant near Mangwon Market with one part-time employee. In early June, she saw a notice at the Mangwon-dong community center asking for volunteers to pack and deliver lunch boxes to older residents. She attended an orientation last Tuesday and helped label 38 containers with delivery addresses. The next available shift is Saturday, June 13, from 9 a.m. to noon. Her restaurant usually opens at 4 p.m., but Saturdays also involve receiving a chicken delivery, preparing sauces and checking supplies before the evening rush. Her employee can accept the delivery, though they have not done it alone before. The volunteer coordinator said Mi-hyun could sign up for one Saturday a month rather than every week. She has the form at home and is looking at the restaurant calendar before choosing a shift.

name: Kim Yu-jin
occupation: Junior marketing coordinator at a skincare brand with an office in Seongsu-dong, Seoul
topic: Putting together a photo slideshow for a friend’s wedding
core_concern: Kim Yu-jin needs to decide which photos to include and finish the slideshow before the wedding hall’s submission deadline.
background: Kim Yu-jin’s university friend Min-ji is getting married on June 20 at a wedding hall in Yeouido. Yu-jin offered to make a short photo slideshow to play while guests arrive. The hall has asked for a 16:9 MP4 file by June 10, no longer than three minutes. Yu-jin has collected about 80 photos through a KakaoTalk group chat, including university trips, birthdays, and a few pictures of the couple together. Min-ji’s sister has also sent childhood photos, but Yu-jin has not yet received anything from the groom’s side. She made a first draft on her laptop after work at the skincare brand’s Seongsu-dong office. It runs nearly five minutes, and several photos are too blurry for the venue’s large screen. She plans to ask Min-ji which moments matter most before cutting it down.

name: Kim Jung-ja
occupation: Owner of a side-dish stall at Mangwon Market in Seoul
topic: Preparing for the Korean Cuisine Cook Certificate (한식조리기능사)
core_concern: Kim Jung-ja wants to decide when to take the written exam and how to fit practical lessons around the stall’s busiest days.
background: Kim Jung-ja, 55, runs a small banchan stall at Mangwon Market in Seoul. She opens at 8 a.m. and usually sells out of spinach namul and braised tofu before the evening rush. After several customers asked whether she could prepare dishes for family gatherings, she began looking into the Korean Cuisine Cook Certificate to strengthen her cooking skills. In late May, she bought a written-exam workbook and started reviewing food safety questions for 30 minutes after closing. She has also found a practical course at a cooking academy near Hapjeong Station that meets twice a week for six weeks. Tuesdays are difficult because she shops for ingredients early that morning, but her younger sister can cover the stall on some afternoons. She is comparing class dates with the exam schedule before paying the course fee.

name: Park Hyun-joo
occupation: Assistant manager at a KB Kookmin Bank branch in Yatap-dong, Seongnam
topic: Growing cherry tomatoes on an apartment balcony
core_concern: Hyun-joo is deciding whether her two tomato plants need larger pots before the summer heat arrives.
background: Park Hyun-joo lives with her husband in an apartment near Yatap Station. On May 10, she bought two cherry tomato seedlings for 3,000 won each at a neighborhood plant shop and put them in separate 15-liter pots on their southeast-facing balcony. The plants get direct sun from about 8 a.m. until noon. Her husband attached bamboo stakes after one stem began leaning, and a colleague at the bank gave her a small bag of tomato fertilizer. By May 24, both plants had flower clusters, but roots were visible through a drainage hole in one pot. The balcony is only 1.2 meters deep, and she keeps trays under the pots so water does not drip onto the apartment below. She has found two 25-liter pots at a store in Seohyeon and is considering whether to move the plants now or leave them until fruit appears.

name: Kim Do-hyun
occupation: 2D art intern at Moru Games, a small mobile-game studio in Daejeon’s Yuseong-gu
topic: Selling pixel-art stickers featuring Daejeon landmarks as a side business
core_concern: He wants to decide whether a small print run and a weekend market stall would be a sensible way to test demand before opening an online shop.
background: Kim Do-hyun, 28, lives in Daejeon and works as a 2D art intern at Moru Games, a six-person studio near KAIST. Outside work, he has drawn pixel-art versions of Daejeon Station, Expo Bridge, and the Hanbat Arboretum. A friend who runs a stationery shop in Eunhaeng-dong suggested turning the drawings into stickers. Kim has ordered sample sheets from a local printer; the colours look good, but the smallest full order is 100 sheets at about ₩1,400 each. He is considering selling them for ₩3,500 a sheet at a weekend craft market in May 2026, then opening a Naver Smart Store if people buy them. His friend can lend him a display rack, but he still needs to account for packaging, stall fees, and unsold stock. All three drawings were made on his own equipment, outside studio hours.

name: Kim Min-a
occupation: First-year student at Byeollae High School in Namyangju
topic: Planning a Saturday reunion with three friends from middle school
core_concern: Kim Min-a is deciding where the group should meet and what they can fit in before one friend has to leave for an academy class.
background: Kim Min-a, 16, lives in Namyangju and has not seen three of her former Byeollae Middle School classmates together since they entered different high schools in March. They have agreed in their KakaoTalk group chat to meet on Saturday, May 23, near Byeollae Station. One friend now attends school in Dasan, another lives closer to Guri, and the third has a math academy class at 5 p.m. Min-a suggested meeting at 1 p.m. for tteokbokki, then taking pictures at a nearby photo booth. Two friends would rather start at a café so they can sit and catch up before going anywhere else. They have found a café with drinks around 5,000 won and a snack place about ten minutes away on foot. No one has booked or reserved anything. Min-a is checking whether the group can do both without rushing the friend who needs to leave early.

name: Kim Hwa-ja
occupation: Retired mail-sorting clerk at Namyangju Post Office
topic: Arranging a June swimming class around her granddaughter’s Tuesday school pickup
core_concern: Kim Hwa-ja needs to decide whether to change swimming classes so she can reliably pick up her granddaughter at 4 p.m.
background: Kim Hwa-ja lives in Namyangju and retired from the mail-sorting room at Namyangju Post Office eight years ago. She has registered for a swimming class at a community center in Byeollae that meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 2:30 to 3:30 p.m., starting June 9. Her daughter recently changed shifts at work and asked Kim to pick up her nine-year-old granddaughter from an elementary school in Dasan every Tuesday at 4 p.m. The trip from the pool usually takes about 35 minutes by bus, leaving almost no time to change clothes or account for delays. Kim has checked the center’s timetable and found two places left in a morning class, but she must request the change by June 5. Her daughter can arrange another pickup on June 9, though not every week. Kim has written the class times and bus route in her calendar and is deciding what to keep.

name: Seo In-hye
occupation: Owner of a small independent bookstore near Sang-dong Station in Bucheon
topic: Organizing a neighborhood book swap
core_concern: She needs to settle the book-swap rules and decide what to do with leftover books.
background: Seo In-hye, 31, owns a small independent bookstore on a side street near Sang-dong Station in Bucheon, Gyeonggi-do. She has had bipolar disorder for many years. Her shop is helping organize a neighborhood book swap on Saturday, June 13, 2026, in the meeting room of a nearby apartment complex. A resident committee member has reserved the room from 2 to 5 p.m., and a local café has offered paper cups and iced barley tea. In-hye has collected 46 books so far, mostly novels and children’s picture books, and two neighbors have volunteered to label tables. The committee expects around 25 visitors, including families from the complex and customers from the bookstore. They still need to decide whether people can take a book without bringing one, and how to handle any leftover books when the room closes.

name: Hong Su-hyun
occupation: CAD/CAM dental technician at Hanbit Dental Laboratory near Bucheon City Hall Station
topic: Moving into a one-room apartment near Sang-dong Station
core_concern: She is deciding which furniture to bring and how much to budget for moving costs.
background: Hong Su-hyun, 25, currently shares a two-bedroom apartment with her older sister near Songnae Station in Bucheon. On May 16, 2026, she is due to move into a small one-room near Sang-dong Station, about 20 minutes from the dental lab where she works. The new place has a ₩5 million deposit and ₩550,000 monthly rent, plus building fees. She paid the holding deposit last week and measured the wall beside the window for a narrow desk and a shelving unit. Her sister has offered to help carry boxes, while Su-hyun is comparing the cost of a small moving van with making several trips by taxi. The landlord said she can install removable curtains but should leave the wallpaper as it is. She has a substance use problem: long-term heavy drinking with several failed attempts to cut down. She has started sorting her belongings and still needs to decide what will fit.
